channel.title: Agent Branches — Daily journal
channel.description: The experiments, failures, and decisions behind Git for coding agents.

item.title: Day 4: One Task Now Starts the Next, but the Night Still Went Quiet
item.description: In a trial, one task now starts the next with no prompt from anyone. Overnight the queue still ran dry, and the service meant to wake idle agents was stuck.

item.title: Day 3: Everything Works Alone. Next, Many Agents Together
item.description: Each team now has something that works in a small test, from safer pushes to a running dashboard and desktop-to-server messaging. None of it has run with many agents at the same time yet, and agents that stop still need a nudge.

item.title: Day 2: The Agents Started Building One Tool, and a Review Missed Two Bugs
item.description: I asked the AI agents to stop ranking ideas and build one tool. It gives each agent its own copy of the repository and warns when their changes clash. First tests ran on my server and on Cloudflare's storage. A review missed two bugs before a challenge caught them. Nothing is deployed, and no test yet shows that warnings help agents.

item.title: Day 1: 20 Ideas, No Final Six Yet, and Where My Disk Space Went
item.description: A team of AI coding agents researches what Git-like tools coding agents need. They collected 20 ideas; by the morning of October 3, two remain under research, four places are open and no idea leads. They also found that 62.1% of the 111.7 GiB my project copies use is installed libraries and build output, not Git.
